tagline: From the lava fields up the valley to Idaho's highest peak.
intro: From Carey, a farm town on the Little Wood River, the highway runs northeast through the northwestern corner of Craters of the Moon, past lava flows as young as 2,000 years, to Arco on the Big Lost River.

There US 93 turns north up the Lost River Valley, through farmland under the Lost River Range, which holds nine of Idaho's twelve highest peaks. The valley narrows as the road nears Mount Borah, then winds through Grandview Canyon toward Idaho 75 near Challis.

moments.title: Craters of the Moon
moments.text: Sixty separate lava flows lie along the Great Rift here, with spatter cones, lava tubes and the hollow molds of trees the lava burned.

moments.title: Arco
moments.text: For about an hour in July 1955 Arco became the first town lit by nuclear power, and every high school class since 1920 has painted its year on Number Hill.

moments.title: Borah Peak
moments.text: Idaho's highest summit, 12,662 feet, went without a name until it was found to beat Hyndman Peak, and the 1983 earthquake raised it about a foot.
